outputNotInScope.default:
Based on your answers, your organisation is likely **not in scope of NIS2**.

Note: a member state may still identify an organisation (Art. 2(2) NIS2). In addition, customers that are in scope may impose requirements on the security of their supply chain (Art. 21(2)(d) NIS2).

In the Netherlands, NIS2 is implemented in the [Cyberbeveiligingswet (Cbw)](https://www.digitaleoverheid.nl/overzicht-van-alle-onderwerpen/cybersecurity/kaders-voor-cybersecurity/cyberbeveiligingswet/). This outcome is indicative; consult the law and the competent supervisory authority for your sector.

outputNotInScopeSmall.title: Outcome
outputNotInScopeSmall.default:
Based on your answers, your organisation is likely **not in scope of NIS2** because of its size.

Note: a small organisation is still in scope if, for example, it is the sole provider of a service that is essential for critical societal or economic activities, if a disruption of its service could have a significant impact on public safety or public health, or if it could induce a systemic risk (Art. 2(2)(b) to (e) NIS2). The member state identifies such organisations. In addition, customers that are in scope may impose requirements on the security of their supply chain.

In the Netherlands, NIS2 is implemented in the [Cyberbeveiligingswet (Cbw)](https://www.digitaleoverheid.nl/overzicht-van-alle-onderwerpen/cybersecurity/kaders-voor-cybersecurity/cyberbeveiligingswet/). This outcome is indicative; consult the law and the competent supervisory authority for your sector.

outputPublicAdmin.title: Outcome
outputPublicAdmin.default:
Whether regional, local and other public administration entities fall under NIS2 is decided by the member state. Public administration entities at regional level fall under NIS2 if, following a risk-based assessment, they provide services the disruption of which could have a significant impact on critical societal or economic activities (Art. 2(2)(f)(ii) NIS2). In that case they are an important entity (Art. 3(2) NIS2). The member state may also apply NIS2 to public administration entities at local level (Art. 2(5)(a) NIS2). Their classification then follows from national law. Consult the Cyberbeveiligingswet to check whether your organisation has been designated.

In the Netherlands, NIS2 is implemented in the [Cyberbeveiligingswet (Cbw)](https://www.digitaleoverheid.nl/overzicht-van-alle-onderwerpen/cybersecurity/kaders-voor-cybersecurity/cyberbeveiligingswet/). This outcome is indicative; consult the law and the competent supervisory authority for your sector.

outputDomainRegistration.title: Outcome
outputDomainRegistration.default:
Based on your answers, your organisation falls under NIS2 as a **provider of domain name registration services** (Art. 2(4) NIS2). On that basis alone it is not an essential or important entity (Art. 3(3) NIS2), but it does have specific obligations, among other things:

- **Registration obligation**: submit information to the competent authority (Art. 3(4) NIS2) and to the registry of ENISA (Art. 27 NIS2);
- **Domain name registration data**: collect accurate and complete registration data and maintain it in a dedicated database, make non-personal registration data publicly available and respond to requests from legitimate access seekers without undue delay (Art. 28 NIS2).

If your organisation also carries out other activities from Annex I or II of NIS2 (for example as a DNS service provider), it may also be an essential or important entity for those activities.

In the Netherlands, NIS2 is implemented in the [Cyberbeveiligingswet (Cbw)](https://www.digitaleoverheid.nl/overzicht-van-alle-onderwerpen/cybersecurity/kaders-voor-cybersecurity/cyberbeveiligingswet/). This outcome is indicative; consult the law and the competent supervisory authority for your sector.

q1.ui:description: NIS2 applies to organisations that provide their services or carry out their activities in the EU. In the Netherlands, NIS2 is implemented in the Cyberbeveiligingswet (Cbw, Cybersecurity Act). Providers of DNS services, top-level domain name registries, domain name registration services, cloud computing, data centre and content delivery network services, managed (security) service providers, online marketplaces, online search engines and social networking services platforms that are not established in the EU but offer services in the EU must designate a representative in the EU (Art. 26(3) NIS2).

q2.ui:description: These categories always fall under NIS2, whatever the size of the organisation (Art. 2(2) to (4) NIS2). For some of them, the size still determines whether the organisation is an essential or an important entity (Art. 3 NIS2): for example, qualified trust service providers are always an essential entity, while for non-qualified trust service providers the size determines the classification. If more than one category applies, choose the first one that applies.
ui:enumTooltips: For example a provider of qualified electronic signatures, the registry of a top-level domain (such as .nl) or a DNS service provider (for authoritative DNS services, operators of root name servers are excluded).

Ministries and other entities of central government. Not included: the judiciary, parliaments and central banks (Art. 6(35) NIS2), and public administration entities that carry out activities in the areas of national security, public security, defence or law enforcement (Art. 2(7) NIS2).
An entity identified as a critical entity under the CER Directive (EU) 2022/2557, in the Netherlands the Critical Entities Resilience Act (Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten).

The member state can identify an organisation regardless of its size, for example if it is the sole provider of an essential service in the member state, if a disruption could have a significant impact on public safety, public security or public health, if it could induce a significant systemic risk, or if the organisation is critical because of its specific importance at national or regional level.
For example telecom operators and internet service providers.
A trust service provider that is not (yet) qualified.
For example a registrar or reseller that registers domain names on behalf of customers. If your organisation is also a top-level domain name registry or DNS service provider, choose the first option.
